issue_context.title: PDF rendering problem: Checkboxes have black background
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
[Erstattung von Arbeitgeberaufwendungen nach __ 56 Abs. 1 und 57, 58 Infektionsschutzgesetz - Antrag(1).pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/6009589/Erstattung.von.Arbeitgeberaufwendungen.nach.__.56.Abs.1.und.57.58.Infektionsschutzgesetz.-.Antrag.1.pdf)

Also available at: [formularserver.bayern.de](https://formularserver.bayern.de/intelliform/forms/stmi+regierungen/rof/b5/55.2/rof_55.2-086/index)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: FF 85.0.2 and FF 86.0b9
- Operating system and its version: Win 10
- PDF.js version: 
FF 85.0.2:
const pdfjsVersion = '2.7.345';
const pdfjsBuild = 'b194c820b';

FF 86.0b9:
const pdfjsVersion = '2.7.510';
const pdfjsBuild = '631bada0d';

- Is a browser extension:
no
Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. load pdf document

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
This is with latest Chrome:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/584660/108499622-e2360880-72ae-11eb-82a7-b181619ff079.png)


What went wrong? (add screenshot)
The checkboxes for e.g. "Geschlecht" are black and you cannot see which one is checked. But this is true for every checkbox in that document.
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/584660/108499753-14e00100-72af-11eb-89d3-1f5ca652e058.png)

Link to a viewer (if hosted on a site other than mozilla.github.io/pdf.js or as Firefox/Chrome extension):
comments:
A black square is drawn on the canvas and then because of transparency here:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/web/annotation_layer_builder.css#L48
we see it.
@timvandermeij, should we replace the color by an opaque one ?

I'm confused about where we actually draw a black square? Looking at https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/web/annotation_layer_builder.css#L48 the color is light blue as intended...

*Edit:* Ah, you probably mean that the PDF file itself contains operations to draw a black square for the checkboxes, and because our overlay is transparent it's not visible. In that case I don't see a problem with making this the same color but opaque instead of transparent.

> In that case I don't see a problem with making this the same color but opaque instead of transparent.

Wouldn't that cause more issues in *general* though, since it will cause anything which is rendered "below" the field to be completely covered up?
For this particular PDF file, such a change would e.g. lead to the bottom of the field descriptions being covered up.
Good point. I wonder how/if other PDF files handle this file then, for example Adobe Reader.

review_comments:
The borders seem thicker now in the reference tests; it looks like the borders are applied twice now, once here and once in existing CSS perhaps?

Moreover, when opening `annotation-text-widget.pdf` from the test suite and clicking the combs field, the border is now extended behind the field (due to the way padding works for the combs fields). Would it maybe be a solution to make the border, just like the background, transparent on focus?

The container and the element had a border and so I just removed the one from the element.
About the focus issue on the comb field, I just removed https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/93ed4bfa119fe82c1fe1fe9cd7d08b1ae719b49e/web/annotation_layer_builder.css#L144-L152 which seems to be useless now (something has likely been fixed in Firefox) and without any consequence with the pdf in #12865.

Is this `makeHexColor`-call *supposed* to use `data.color` now, since naively I'd assume that it should actually use `borderColor` (defined just above) instead?
As-is the borderColor is being ignored, which I'm assuming wasn't intended; was this perhaps fallout from addressing one of the review comments?

`borderColor` is set from `MK-BC` entry and `color` is set from `C` one.
If I understand the spec correctly, `BC` (see https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/pdf/pdfs/PDF32000_2008.pdf#page=417) is optional and for widget annotations, when `C` (see https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/pdf/pdfs/PDF32000_2008.pdf#page=392) is for icon, popup and link, so only one of the `BC` and `C` should be set.
If I'm correct, I should likely add a comment.
